title: Degree of the Bonami even part
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional Boolean cube, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. If the Fourier degree of $f$ is at most $k$, then the Fourier degree of the function on $\{\pm1\}^n$ obtained by averaging the two first-coordinate slices of $f$ is also at most $k$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional Boolean cube
The Fourier degree of $f$ is at most $k$
